title: Beam with flexible (semi-rigid) and pinned end connections: stiffness coefficients

source.work: McGuire, W., Gallagher, R. H., Ziemian, R. D., Matrix Structural Analysis
source.notes: input data and targets read on the cited pages; nothing of the source is reproduced

analysis: Plane (x-y) problem of the source modelled in 3D with the global Y axis vertical, so that the source's x, y and theta_z are the model's X, Y and rz. In-plane bending is about local z for every member (default orientation), hence the source's I is the section's Iz. The source gives the stiffness matrix of a beam with rotational springs k1 = alpha1 EI/L and k2 = alpha2 EI/L at its ends (Eq. 13.31) and the special cases of a pin at end 1 (Eq. 13.32) and at end 2 (Eq. 13.33). Numeric instance chosen here: L = 6 m, E = 200 kN/mm^2, I = 200e6 mm^4, alpha1 = 3, alpha2 = 6. Three separate members between fully held nodes: 'semi' (n1-n2) with partial rz releases (springs k1 at end i, k2 at end j), 'pin1' (n3-n4) with a full rz release at end i, 'pin2' (n5-n6) with a full rz release at end j. Combination V imposes v = 1 mm at the first node of each member, combination R a rotation of 0.001 rad there; the reactions are the first and second columns of the printed matrices times the imposed displacement (zero coefficients are not listed as targets). First order, no shear deformation. Section properties the source does not give because they do not enter its plane model (Iy, J; A where stated) are placeholders that do not influence the targets.
